M-PORTABLE-EXPORT.Summary: Explicit on-demand export of generated portal pages into portal/published. Interactive mode retains bundled search, embedded fonts and portable controls. Static mode creates complete independently relocatable en/ru editions with local assets, light-only colors, no JavaScript, native topic/section links, inline workflow-stage descriptions and standalone diagram views. Both use validated file links and owned output replacement; neither builds nor deploys the hosted site. The Hub (v2) has its own packer, aicc/v2/tools/package.py: aicc-v2-hub (both editions), aicc-v2-hub-ru and aicc-v2-hub-en, each the built site that opens from files plus the full source and the drawn diagrams.

M-PORTAL-SOURCE.Summary: Editable bilingual AICC portal source: language-specific charter and explanatory Markdown, shared UI messages and authored chrome, source selection, and the complete-site build/check tools. The build also composes the independent neighbouring sections without importing their content into the charter corpus. Beside it, the Hub (version 2) is its own package at aicc/v2: Russian Markdown pages, project cards, vocabulary, the Справочник data, learning maps, the PI calendar and the scenario catalog, with its own build, site check, browser check and offline packer; it does not read the v1 sources.

M-PORTAL-NEIGHBOURS.Summary: Common O!Bank presentation and navigation for the language routers and the five branches Center, Discovery Catalog, Portfolio, Program and AI Lab. portal/tools/router.py renders each router with one door per branch and a fact counted from the branch's sources; the shell offers branch search and a global scope over every branch index, on by default on the router; renamed routes keep their page references. Discovery renders its pages with portal/tools/discovery.py from the bilingual Markdown records in portfolio/{en,ru}/discovery/ and projects them into shared context, grouped navigation and expandable scenario cards; workflow previews link to source stages. AI Lab projects the complete operating model from lab/{en,ru}/lab.md with a source-keyed, freshness-checked Russian edition, a six-stage/five-lane matrix with accessible focus/reset controls, both operating systems, capabilities, intent loop and illustrative guardrail scorecard. Shared portal/tools/kanban.py helpers and kanban.css/js present compact native record cards, consistent equal-width column headers and one selected inline summary below the active view. Selection, replacement, keyboard activation, dismissal and hidden-selection clearing are identical for Portfolio and Program delivery; no operational state is stored in the browser. Secondary record content uses disclosures, with decision limitations visible. Portfolio projects the maintained Registry into a dated role-safe board, review queue, Standing Initiatives, roadmap, register, gate guidance and eleven record-derived progress summaries. Backlog, Briefs, board, Dashboard and source-language agreement are checked before publication; shared capacity, Waiting context, ordinary/standing separation and unknown observations retain their charter meaning. The Registry owns state and evidence; browser controls only filter and reveal views. Program projects the maintained Program Backlog through portal/tools/delivery.py into a five-column, three-service-class Program Kanban, Portfolio intake relationships and complete native project documents. Registry-derived states, parent admission, Waiting context, board placement, counts and shared limits are validated; the current Program Backlog is empty. INI-013 records the existing service-resolution proposal in the Portfolio Funnel, without a business-case approval or delivery admission. A stable project mapping connects its goal and progress summary to its working documents. Program projects the bilingual service-resolution documents from portfolio/{en,ru}/projects/service-resolution/ into an overview and eleven child documents, retaining all text, tables, code, diagram labels and geometry, intra-project destinations and section search. Scoped native diagram controls support expansion, pan, zoom, fit, actual size and focus return. Section content ownership, search and lifecycle remain separate; explicit Registry-derived Initiative/project relationships connect Portfolio and Program in addition to the common shell. The Portfolio and Program views read the working state from portfolio/{en,ru}/ and decisions from registry/{en,ru}/ (DR-2026-065).

M-PORTAL-PROJECTION.Summary: One generated static package under html/aicc. The root index.html opens the AI Competence Hub (v2/ru/index.html) and lists both versions. v1/ holds the frozen Competence Center portal: per language a router and the five branches center/, discovery/, portfolio/, program/ and lab/, with its source files; the former {lang}/ addresses at the root forward into v1. v2/ holds the Hub in Russian (ru/, assets/, sources/), built from aicc/v2. Never edited by hand. The Hub has two editions from one design: v2/ru (the source) and v2/en (its translation, page for page, with a language switch on every page); /aicc/ opens the Russian edition.

M-AICC-DEPLOY.Summary: Rust command-line tool that checks the generated site, mirrors html/aicc into the clean deploy repository, writes a hashed manifest, and with an explicit flag commits, pushes origin then websvc, and verifies the served manifest. Dry run by default.

M-PORTAL-LOCALIZATION.Summary: Language source identity and comparison, reviewed translation selection, source freshness, stable structure, record identity checks, and paired table extraction for generated views. English lookup paths do not establish language precedence. In the Hub (v2) Russian is the source language; industry terms carry their English form through the vocabulary markers. For the Hub (v2): tools/i18n.py gives every interface string, plural, month and data field in the edition language (Russian passes through unchanged); tools/parity.py holds English to Russian page for page (anchors, components, progress keys, tables, links), finds Russian left on English pages, and reports translations older than their Russian source by recorded hashes.
